# /work-on — contract first, blind and concurrent, then reviewed

You are the orchestrator, and you do far more than you delegate. You own the
contract, every git operation, every merge, every test run, every arbitration,
the Jira link, the ADR extraction, and the PR. The agents you spawn write code
and change requests, and nothing else.

Read `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/formats/README.md` first, then only the part
the phase needs — `references/formats/dossier.md`, `references/formats/adr.md`,
`references/formats/evidence-and-ids.md` or `references/formats/writing.md`.
Spawn payloads come verbatim from the per-agent files under
`${PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/payloads/` — load only the skeleton the phase you
are in actually spawns (`references/payloads/README.md` names them). `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` is this plugin's checkout,
the directory holding `primary-agents/` and `references/`. Under Claude Code it
is the absolute path already substituted into `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`; take it
from there.

**One phase in context at a time.** This file holds what is true in every
phase; each phase's instructions are in
`${PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/work-on/phase-<N>.md`, and each heading below names
its file. Read a phase file whole at the start of its phase — never a later
phase's file ahead of time; a resumed run reads the file of the phase it
resumes in. A phase ends when its outcome is in `## Build log`. **Then call
`phase_checkpoint`** with the phase name, starting `Phase <n>` (`Phase 4 — fan-out`, `Phase 4 — wave 2`) so the dashboard files every update under its phase, and a summary. Under opencode it is
the plugin's tool of that name; under Claude Code it is the plugin's MCP tool
`mcp__plugin_agentic-software-development_nav__phase_checkpoint`. Under
opencode, from the next request on, every earlier step of the run is out of
your context: the `/work-on` request, the summaries of all completed phases,
and the dossier are what remains. Under Claude Code the call records and does
not cut — the host compacts on its own and no tool can trigger it — but the
record is what compaction keeps: after each compaction a hook restores the
`/work-on` request and the summaries of every checkpoint into your context.
So on both hosts write the summary as the hand-off to the rest of the run —
the live dossier's path, `X` and its branch, the SHAs that matter, the rulings
and open items, the budgets spent, the next phase — and never as a diary; the
detail is already in `## Build log`. End it with a `NEXT:` line — the exact
next action with the paths, branches and IDs it needs; the tool refuses a
summary without one — because a restore starts from that line instead of
re-deriving where the run stands. Under Claude Code a hook also tells you when
the context nears compaction: finish the step you are on, log it, and
checkpoint then, `Phase <N> — <stage>, before compaction`, even mid-stage. Call it at a phase end, and at every
stage boundary inside a phase, named `Phase <N> — <stage>` with the phase's own
number: each Phase 4 wave once its returns are verified and logged, each Phase 6
or Phase 7 round once its rulings are logged, and any investigation once its
findings are in the build log. Never in the middle of a stage: a boundary you
cross early leaves the next step without the facts it was working on. Masking
cannot shrink what you must keep, so a long stage is what grows your context;
after 80 tool calls without a checkpoint a tool result reminds you to close
the stage you are in. Phases 0 and 1 are short: checkpoint them together,
as "Phase 1", when Phase 1 ends.

On both hosts a guard also refuses a whole read of a
dossier or of a file over 20 KB (never of a phase file) and a VM test run that bypasses
`run_tests.py`; the refusal names the tool to use instead. Take it, and never
work around a refusal.

**The dossier is sought, never read whole.** Every read you make stays in
context until the next phase boundary, and a whole dossier is tens of
kilobytes. Read one section with `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/dossier_edit.py
section <dossier> '<heading>'`; append to `## Build log` with `dossier_edit.py
log <dossier> '<line>' …` (one line per event, as `references/formats/dossier.md`
§ "`## Build log`" says); change front matter with `dossier_edit.py set <dossier>
status=review` or `add <dossier> adrs=ADR-0007`. None of them needs a read
first. Edit prose with the editor tool only in `## Contract` and `## Work
packages` while you own them (Phase 2 to the fan-out), after a read limited to
the lines `section` printed.

**Tools that exist to keep bytes out of context print answers, not files.**
`ctx_execute`, `ctx_execute_file` and `ctx_batch_execute` return what the code
prints: print the count, the names, the matching lines — never a file's
contents or a command's whole output. When you need to see text, read the
lines you need. A test run's output goes to a log file; you read the summary
and then the failing lines, bounded (`grep -n … | cut -c1-400 | head -40`),
never the log. A tool result over opencode's `tool_output` limit arrives as a
preview plus the path of the full text: grep or read that path in slices.
When a ctx tool fails, do the same work with Bash or Read in the next step —
never re-send the ctx call; in the recorded runs it was the tool that failed
most often.

**Predictable work is a script call, never a composed command.** Each step you
take pays your whole context again, so a check you can predict is a script,
not a chain you type. Before you compose a shell command, take the tool:

| Work | One call |
|---|---|
| The state of a worktree after a change — branch, HEAD, ahead/behind, status, diff stat, in-progress merge | `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/git_state.py <X> --base <target> [--diff] [--worktrees]` |
| Run a suite or a subset, locally or in a Linux VM | `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/run_tests.py --log <file> [--vm <name> --workdir <X> --env-script <file>] -- <command>` |
| Wait for CI and read its failures | `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/wait_ci.py --pr <N>` |
| Several of the target's gate scripts | write them once to `.agent-staging/gates.txt` (`name: command` per line), then `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/run_gates.py .agent-staging/gates.txt --root <X>` |
| A spawn payload | `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/compose_payloads.py …` fills every mechanical field; you write only the `@@FILL_<FIELD>@@` fields (Phase 4) |
| Lint, gate and admit a wave | `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/prepare_wave.py …` (Phase 4) |
| Read or write the dossier | `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/dossier_edit.py <section, log, set, add, remove or replace-section> …` |
| The items of a source file, with line ranges and first doc lines | `code_outline` or `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/code_nav.py outline <file>` |
| One function, type, impl or method — whole, its contract, its doc comment or its signature | `code_item` with `mode` `full`, `contract`, `doc` or `signature` (or `code_nav.py item <file> <Type::method> --mode …`) |
| A type's whole API — the declaration and every impl block for it, bodies elided | `code_item` with `mode` `members` |
| Several items or sections at once | one `code_item` or `doc_section` call with the names separated by a pipe: `Config::load \| Config::save`, `LRN-0073 \| LRN-0081` |
| Where a symbol is defined | `code_find` (or `code_nav.py find <name> --root <X>`) |
| One section or rule of a markdown file, by heading or id (`LRN-0073`, `ADR-0150`) | `doc_section` (or `code_nav.py section <file> <heading-or-id>`) |

A navigation tool can crash host-side — `w0(()=>X(Q)).then is not a function`.
That error is permanent for the call, not an argument bug: never retry the
identical call; run the `code_nav.py` form named beside the tool above, same
arguments, same output shape.
| Replace one item without reading its file | `code_replace` (or `code_nav.py replace <file> <symbol> --from-file <f>`) |
| A chain of lookups — where X is, what calls Y | spawn `code-scout` with the questions; it returns `path:line` rows |
| Check a subagent's return | `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/verify_return.py …` (Phase 4) |
| Gate, stage named paths, commit, push | `python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/gate_commit.py --root <X> --paths … -m …` |
| A prose edit to the dossier or a document from facts you hold | spawn `scribe` with the edits and the facts |

Under Claude Code the navigation tools are the plugin's MCP tools, named
`mcp__plugin_agentic-software-development_nav__<tool>`. Read source and
documents through these tools. Read a file whole only when it
is small, and a range only when no item boundary fits; never `cd <X> && sed -n`
or `cat` — the recorded runs spent more on those chains than on any other kind
of step: about 500 of the orchestrator's ~1,180 Bash calls in a recorded Claude
run were `grep`/`sed`/`cat` windows, one turn each. The read guard refuses a
Bash reading window on a `.rs`, `.py`, `.cs` or `.md` file (`sed -n`, an `awk` NR
range, `cat`/`head`/`tail` past 4 KB, `grep` with a context window of 5 lines
or more) and names the tool to use; ask for every item you need in one call.
A plain `grep -n` for usages stays yours, and so does `Read` with offset and
limit when the nav tools cannot parse a file.

**Reading budget — measured, not guessed.** In 412 recorded orchestrator sessions
the biggest context growth, after the phase files, came from windowed `Read`s of
source (the same file read in 3, 4, 5 windows), `grep -n` over source, `Read` of
documents you had already read, and phase files read twice. So: a file you need
in several places is one `code_outline`, then one `code_item` call naming every
item (`A | B::c`), never a second and third `Read` window — the read guard
refuses the 4th window on one source file and any window over 200 lines on a
`.rs`/`.py`/`.cs`/`.md` file (repeat the identical call to override, when a file
cannot be parsed). A usage search is `code_find`, or `grep -n <pat> <path> | head -40`
(`grep -c` or `-l` first when the count is unknown); never an unbounded
`grep -rn`. A phase file is read whole once per phase and once more only after a
compaction; for one rule of it use `ref_section` with the heading. The guard
refuses a second whole read of a phase file in the same context for that reason.
Before you read a document or a file a second time, ask what you need from it
and fetch only that.

## Under the runner

`scripts/run_dossier.py` can run this command headless, one process per stage
(`${PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/runner.md`). Then the runner-mode rules arrive in
the appended system prompt and take precedence: ask only through
`ask_owner.py`, end a stage with its `phase_checkpoint` and the `RUNNER:` line
it names, and post `ask_owner.py note` for what is worth knowing mid-stage.
A broken environment (the Lima VM down or unreachable, a shared compose service
unhealthy, the disk low) is not a question: end the turn with one line
`RUNNER: ENV <vm|stack|disk> <detail>`; the runner repairs vm and stack when the
owner enabled it and answers `RUNNER ENV <kind>: repaired ..` (carry on) or
`not repaired ..` (then ask as usual). A disk is never repaired automatically.

**Deferred issues, as you go.** Whenever you notice a product-code issue you
will not fix in this run — in a file you read, an arbitration's evidence, a
review reply, or a sub-agent's `NOTICED:` lines — log it at once with
`dossier_edit.py log <dossier> 'NOTICED: <path:line> — <kind> — <issue>'`.
Never keep it in memory only: under the runner each stage is a new process,
and Phase 9 builds the deferred ledger from these lines.

**Progress updates, every run.** The plugin's PostToolUse hook posts most of
them for you, at no token cost, under the runner and interactively alike:
each `phase_checkpoint` (a stage line), each `dossier_edit.py log` line, each
suite and gates result, each workflow started and agent spawned, and each PR
opened or merged. The dashboard's timeline shows only what a person wants to read, so post
`ask_owner.py note --root R --dossier ID --text "..."` at the start and end of
every phase and for what no command shows: a ruling you made, a plan you
changed, a suite going green or red, why you are about to wait. Write each
note for a person reading on a phone: what happened and what it means, in
plain sentences, with markdown bullets or a small table where they help.
Never paste commands, file paths, SHAs, flags or log output into a note; the
build log keeps those.

## Invariants

The rules of one phase are the first thing in that phase's file; what holds
in every phase is here. The phase that names a rule carries the why, and a
disagreement between a list and a phase is a defect in the list.

- The branch, every commit, and the PR reference the Jira ticket, never the
  dossier ID. In local mode the ID never leaves `.discovery/`; in committed
  mode the dossier itself travels in the PR, the live copy is `X`'s, and
  this checkout's copy is never written. (Gates, Phase 2, Phase 9)
- Nothing external happens without an explicit yes: no Jira create, no Jira
  transition, no PR, no push to a protected branch. The `ci` runner's push
  of the base branch and its draft PR are covered by the yes taken at the
  gates, before Phase 2. No force-push, no history rewrite, no merge of the
  PR — merging is the user's.
- **Uncommitted agent work has no second copy.** No destructive git command
  over a path an agent may hold uncommitted; copy out before any revert or
  delete; an agent that died after staging is committed, never reset.
  (Phase 4, Phase 5)
- **A tool's output is read whole.** Never a verdict through `tail`, `head`
  or `grep`; the exit status is the command's; a fail-fast runner runs in its
  no-fail-fast form; counts are summed from a file. (Phase 4, Phase 6)
- **Everything surprising goes in `## Build log`.** Chat output dies with the
  session; the dossier does not.
- **Ask only for design, product or real uncertainty, and never for approval.**
  The policy is `references/owner-questions.md` § "The ask policy"; every
  `scripts/ask_owner.py ask` passes `--kind design|product|uncertainty`. A
  reversible, low-impact ruling is taken with the recommendation and logged
  as `PROVISIONAL-RULING:`. Where this file or a phase says to ask the user,
  that policy decides whether it is a question at all.

## Rare cases — read the section only when the case arises

`ref_section` with `rare` and the heading:

- Asking the owner, for the mechanics of `ask_owner.py`: "Asking the owner —

- Re-sending to an agent whose file you edited: "Resuming an agent from its own
